title: Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Duties

facts.text: Fundamental rights put restrictions on the power of the government.
facts.quote: Fundamental rights put restrictions on the power of the government.

facts.text: Restriction: the State shall not discriminate between and among citizens on the basis of caste, religion, race, language or sex.
facts.quote: State shall not discriminate between and among citizens on the basis of caste, religion, race, language or sex.

facts.text: Restriction: the State shall not deny anybody equality before the law and equal protection of the law.
facts.quote: State shall not deny anybody equality before the law and equal protection of the law.

facts.text: Restriction: no person shall be deprived of his life.
facts.quote: No person shall be deprived of his life.

facts.text: Restriction: the State shall not impose any religious taxes.
facts.quote: State shall not impose any religious taxes.

facts.text: The Constitution gives the State express instructions or guidelines about policies to achieve the goals expressed in the Preamble; hence they are called Directive Principles of State Policy.
facts.quote: The Constitution has given express instructions to the State about what policies it should undertake. This is in the nature of giving directives or guidelines about how to achieve the goals expressed in the Preamble. Hence they are called as Directive Principles of State Policy.

facts.text: When India won independence, it faced a great challenge of establishing order and carrying out smooth administration.
facts.quote: When India won independence, we faced a great challenge of establishing order and carrying out smooth administration.

facts.text: Eradication of poverty, backwardness and illiteracy had to be urgently pursued.
facts.quote: Eradication of poverty, backwardness and illiteracy had to be urgently pursued.

facts.text: India had to be transformed into a developed and progressive nation.
facts.quote: In short, India had to be transformed into a developed and progressive nation.

facts.text: Through the Directive Principles, the Constitution specified the subjects to which the Union and State Governments should give priority for people's welfare; each Directive contains a subject for the State Policy.
facts.quote: The Constitution has specified the subjects to which the Union and State Governments should give priority in their policies for people's welfare through the Directive Principles of State Policy. Each Directive contains a subject for the State Policy.

facts.text: Implementing all the directives at the same time would require a lot of resources, so the makers did not make them binding upon the State like the fundamental rights; States should implement them slowly and steadily.
facts.quote: it would require a lot of resources if all these policies were to be implemented at the same time. That is the reason why they did not make the directives binding upon the State like the fundamental rights. They expected that States should implement them slowly and steadily.

facts.text: Directive: the State should secure adequate means of livelihood to all citizens without any gender discrimination.
facts.quote: The State should secure adequate means of livelihood to all citizens without any gender discrimination.

facts.text: Directive: the State should secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
facts.quote: The State should secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

facts.text: Directive: the State should secure the improvement of public health.
facts.quote: The State should secure the improvement of public health.

facts.text: Directive: the State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and safeguard the forests and wild-life of the country.
facts.quote: The State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and safeguard the forests and wild-life of the country.

facts.text: Directive: the State shall protect all monuments of historic interest and national importance.
facts.quote: The State shall protect all monuments of historic interest and national importance.

facts.text: Directive: the State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, especially the Scheduled Castes and Tribes.
facts.quote: The State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, especially the Scheduled Castes and Tribes.

facts.text: Directive: the State shall offer public assistance to citizens in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, etc.
facts.quote: The State shall offer public assistance to citizens in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, etc.

facts.text: Directive: the State shall secure a uniform civil code applicable to the entire country.
facts.quote: The State shall secure a uniform civil code applicable to the entire country.

facts.text: Foreign Policy directive: it should be the policy of the State to endeavour to secure the promotion of international peace and security.
facts.quote: For example, Foreign Policy : It should be the policy of the State to endeavour to secure the promotion of international peace and security.

facts.text: Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Rights are two sides of the same coin.
facts.quote: Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Rights are two sides of the same coin.

facts.text: Due to Fundamental Rights citizens get the most needed liberty, while Directive Principles create an atmosphere conducive to the growth of democracy.
facts.quote: Due to Fundamental Rights, citizens get the most needed liberty, while Directive Principles of State Policy create an atmosphere conducive to the growth of democracy.

facts.text: We cannot go to the courts if a Directive is not implemented, but we can put pressure on the Government in various ways.
facts.quote: Even though we cannot go to the courts if a Directive is not implemented by the Government, we can put pressure on the Government in various ways to make a policy in order to meet these goals.

facts.text: In a democracy, citizens have a dual responsibility: to be vigilant that their rights are not unfairly restricted and to fulfil some duties and responsibilities.
facts.quote: In a democracy, citizens have a dual responsibility. They should not only be vigilant that their rights are not unfairly restricted, but should also fulfil some duties and responsibilities.

facts.text: The benefits of Government schemes cannot reach all people if they do not fulfil their Fundamental Duties.
facts.quote: The benefits of the various schemes of the Government cannot reach all people if they do not fulfil their Fundamental Duties.

facts.text: Under the Swachch Bharat Scheme the Government implemented several projects, but people too need to change habits that make public places dirty.
facts.quote: the Government has implemented several projects under its Swachch Bharat Scheme, but people, too, need to change their habits that make public places dirty.

facts.text: Fundamental Duties were included in the Constitution so that Indian citizens become conscious of their responsibilities.
facts.quote: In order that the Indian citizens become conscious of their responsibilities, Fundamental Duties were included in the Constitution.

facts.text: Duty: to abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and the National Anthem.
facts.quote: To abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and the National Anthem.

facts.text: Duty: to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
facts.quote: To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.

facts.text: Duty: to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.
facts.quote: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.

facts.text: Duty: to defend the country, and to render national service when called upon to do so.
facts.quote: To defend the country, and to render national service when called upon to do so.

facts.text: Duty: to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood transcending diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
facts.quote: To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood transcending diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

facts.text: Duty: to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
facts.quote: To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.

facts.text: Duty: to protect and improve the natural environment, and to have compassion for living creatures.
facts.quote: To protect and improve the natural environment, and to have compassion for living creatures.

facts.text: Duty: to develop the scientific temper, humanism and spirit of inquiry and reform.
facts.quote: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and spirit of inquiry and reform.

facts.text: Duty: to safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
facts.quote: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.

facts.text: Duty: to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.
facts.quote: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.

facts.text: Duty: every citizen who is a parent or guardian should provide opportunities of education to his or her child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
facts.quote: Every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian should provide opportunities of education to his or her child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

facts.text: Situations where Fundamental Duties are not followed: a boy scribbling on a historical structure, hanging lemon and chillies, damaging a public bus, a woman emptying a garbage can on the street.
facts.quote: A boy scribbling on a historical structure ... Hanging lemon, chillies ... Damaging a public bus ... A woman emptying a garbage can on the street ... Which of the Fundamental Duties are not being followed in the situations above?

facts.text: A child sees the village river full of plastic waste and resolves never to throw any waste in the river.
facts.quote: The river in our village does not look like a river at all! What an amount of plastic waste! Even if anybody tells me, I will never throw any waste in the river.

facts.text: It is our duty to protect the resources and public property of our country.
facts.quote: It is our duty to protect the resources and public property of our country.

facts.text: Resolutions include telling girls and boys to go to school, participating in the festivals of different religions and celebrating them by avoiding pollution of the environment.
facts.quote: Let us tell girls and boys to go to school. ... Let us participate in the festivals of different religions. Let us celebrate them by avoiding pollution of the environment.

facts.text: Girls and boys between the ages 6 and 14 have got the right to education.
facts.quote: Girls and boys between the ages 6 and 14 have got the right to education.

facts.text: Many girls and boys cannot go to school because they have to work to help their parents earn a living.
facts.quote: Yet many girls and boys are not able to go to school because of many reasons. They have to work to help their parents earn a living for the family.

facts.text: Facilities offered by the Government that bring improvements include public toilets, clean water supply and vaccination of children.
facts.quote: Which improvements will be possible with the following facilities offered by the Government? Public toilets, Clean water supply, Vaccination of children
